previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, and a history of DVT, was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for hypotension and significant bleeding from a right thigh wound. Her INR was critically elevated at 7.7 due to warfarin therapy, contributing to hemorrhagic shock. She received multiple blood transfusions, vitamin K, and reversal agents. During her ICU stay, she was aggressively ultrafiltered due to volume overload. Blood cultures revealed viridans streptococci, prompting a two-week course of vancomycin, though repeat cultures were negative and imaging ruled out endocarditis or abscess. A tunneled dialysis catheter was placed after removal of a malfunctioning line, with venography showing patent central veins. Wound care was optimized, and anticoagulation was restarted with warfarin, bridged with heparin. She stabilized, transitioned to the medical floor, and was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing dialysis, wound management, and INR monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with ESRD on HD, DM, h/o DVTs, here 
with MRSA bacteremia, septicemia.  
.
# Fever, MRSA bacteremia, septicemia: High grade MRSA 
bacteremia, due to infection of HD line.  The line was first 
been changed over a wire, but there had been pus at the line 
site and positive blood cultures at the time of this change, so 
there was concern that the new line may not be sterile.  For 
this reason, a temporary line was placed on the opposite side 
and the prior tunnelled line was pulled.  After surveillance 
blood cultures remained negative, this temporary line was 
converted to a new tunnelled line.  The patient remained 
afebrile thereafter.  TEE showed no evidence of endocarditis.  
She is to have a 2 week course of vancomycin from the time this 
new tunnelled line was placed (___), meaning that the last 
day of vancomycin should be ___.  Vancomycin has been dosed 
per HD protocol.  The final sets of surveillance blood cultures 
are negative to date but remain pending at the time of discharge 
and will need to be followed up as an outpatient.  
.
Of note, the patient had an isolated low-grade temperature of 
100.4 >24h prior to discharge.  An additional set of blood 
cultures were drawn, which remain pending at the time of 
discharge.  A chest xray was also done, which showed no evidence 
of pneumonia.  However, it did show a density over the lower 
thoracic spine which may be due to osteophytes or a tortuous, 
calcified aorta.  This finding could have also been consistent 
with an epidural infection, however given the patient's clinical 
stability, lack of back pain, and lack of other new neurologic 
findings on exam, the clinical suspicion for epidural space 
infection was low, so additional imaging was not pursued.  
.
# Abdominal pain: There was concern for cholecystitis on 
admission with positive HIDA scan, but abdominal pain resolved 
quickly and pt has had prior abnormalities on imaging studies 
which were similar.  The surgical team therefore felt that there 
was less concern currently for active cholecystitis.  There are 
currently no plans for surgery or percutaneous cholecystostomy 
tube.  The patient no longer has any abdominal pain, and she has 
been tolerating a regular diet.  It is likely that her pain was 
due to constipation, which has now improved.  
.
# ___ ulcers:  Thigh wounds were concerning for calciphylaxis vs 
pressure ulcers which have not been healing well due to ___ 
edema.  Plastic surgery evaluated the patient and recommended 
wet-to-dry dressing changes bid.    
.
# ESRD on HD: Usual HD schedule is ___.  While she was 
hospitalized, she received daily ultrafiltration to remove 
excess volume.  This was well-tolerated.  We continued her 
regimen of epogen at HD, renagel, nephrocaps, sensipar 
(particularly given concern for possible calciphylaxis).  
Vancomycin was dosed per hemodialysis protocol.  
.

an active gallabladder process.  For this reason, she was 
initially on only half of her home NPH dose.  However, when she

.

hemodialysis.  She was asymptomatic, and the blood pressure 
improved spontaneously without intervention.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with cholecystitis on ultrasound.  Perihepatic
fluid.  Diffuse abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  Right upper quadrant ultrasound from one day prior.  CT of the
abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT scanning of the abdomen and pelvis was performed
after oral and intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
obtained.  Intravenous contrast was requested, and was approved by the
dialysis fellow, with the idea that dialysis would be performed tomorrow
morning.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  The lung bases demonstrate bilateral dependent
atelectasis, worse in the right lower lobe.  The visualized heart is
enlarged; pericardium appears unremarkable.  No focal liver lesions are
identified.  The liver as well as loops of predominantly large bowel extend
laterally due to abdominal wall laxity. There is also a small to
moderate amount of perihepatic fluid seen.

The appearance of the gallbladder is very similar compared to previous
studies; however, there may be a small amount of pericholecystic fluid between
the gallbladder and the liver on the current study.  The gallbladder is at the
upper limits of normal measuring 4 cm. Mild prominence of the common bile duct
is noted, measuring roughly 10-11 mm. There is no stranding in the right upper
quadrant, however. 

The adrenal glands, spleen, pancreas, and kidneys appear unremarkable. There
is no bowel obstruction.  There is a large amount of stool in the rectal
vault.  There is no free air within the abdomen. The caliber of the abdominal
aorta is normal with some atherosclerotic calcification.  There are extensive
anterior abdominal wall venous collaterals.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The bladder is unremarkable.  Again seen, unchanged is a
large fibroid uterus with several calcified fibroids noted.  The adnexa are
not well seen.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  There is
circumferential thickening of the rectal wall, as on prior studies, but
possibly more pronounced. There is an unusual, and also unchanged appearance
to the right common femoral vessels, with extensive localized
venous collaterals in the groin.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions are appreciated.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Moderate amount of perihepatic ascites.

2.  Mild prominence of the common bile duct and gallbladder, which is at the
upper limits of normal in size, but appears similar compared with prior
studies.  Ultrasound earlier today however, was suggestive of acute
cholecystitis.  Clinical correlation is requested.

3.  Fibroid uterus.

4.  Circumferential rectal wall thickening, etiology unclear.  This has
progressed gradually over many years at least back to ___.  Correlation with
proctoscopy may be of benefit.

RADIOLOGISTS:  The procedure was performed by Drs. ___, the
attending radiologist, who was present and supervising throughout.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  The left neck, chest and previously placed tunneled
hemodialysis line were prepped and draped in the standard sterile fashion.  A
pre-procedure timeout was performed.

Using a sterile technique, after the use of approximately 10 mL of 1%
lidocaine local anesthesia, two Amplatz wires were advanced through the lumens
of the hemodialysis catheter under fluoroscopic guidance.  The catheters were
advanced into the IVC.  Blunt dissection was performed in the subcutaneous
tunnel until the cuff of the catheter was exposed.  The hemodialysis catheter
was removed over the Amplatz wires.

A new double-lumen hemodialysis catheter measuring 27 cm tip-to-cuff was
advanced over the two Amplatz wires through the subcutaneous tract and the tip
of the catheter was positioned into the right atrium under fluoroscopic
guidance.  The wires were removed and the catheter was flushed and heplocked.
The catheter was secured to the skin with 0 silk sutures.  A sterile dressing
was applied.  Final fluoroscopic image of the chest demonstrates the tip of
the catheter to be located into the right atrium.  The patient tolerated the
procedure well without immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful exchange of the previously placed tunneled
hemodialysis catheter.  The new catheter measures 27 cm from tip-to-cuff and
the tip is located in the right atrium.  The line is ready for use.

HISTORY:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis,
with high-grade MRSA bacteremia from line infection.  Please remove the left
IJ tunneled HD catheter, and place new right-sided temporary line.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Drs. ___, and ___ performed the procedure.  Dr.
___ attending radiologist, was present and supervised the entire
procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Risks and benefits of the procedure were explained to
the patient, and written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was
placed on the angiographic table supine, and the right neck was prepped and
draped in standard sterile fashion.  Using ultrasound guidance, and after
local anesthesia with 5 cc of 1% lidocaine,  the right external jugular vein
was accessed with a 21-gauge micropuncture needle, and hard copies of
sonographic images before and after venipuncture were obtained.

0.018 guidewire was then placed through the needle, and needle was exchanged
for a 4.5 ___ micropuncture sheath.  Guidewire was then exchanged for 0.025
___ wire, which was advanced into the inferior vena cava under fluoroscopic
guidance.

Neck incision was progressively dilated with 12 and 14 ___ dilators, and
14.5 ___ double-lumen temporary hemodialysis catheter was placed over the
wire, and positioned with its tip in the proximal right atrium.  Wire was then
removed, and both lumens were flushed.  The line was secured to the skin with
0 silk sutures, and sterile dressing was applied.

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of fentanyl and
Versed during the total intraservice time of 45 minutes, during which the
patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.

Following placement of the new right IJ temporary hemodialysis catheter, the
patient was placed in sitting upright in a stretcher, and the left neck and
tunneled catheter were prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion. Sutures
were removed, and the subcutaneous tunnel was anesthetized with 5 cc of 1%
lidocaine.  Using blunt dissection, the catheter hub was removed, and tunneled
line was removed without difficulty.  Pressure was held on the left internal
jugular vein for 5 minutes until hemostasis was achieved.  A sterile dressing
was applied at the skin exit site.  Catheter tip was sent for culture.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Successful placement of temporary double-lumen hemodialysis catheter via
the right external jugular vein, with the catheter tip located in the proximal
right atrium.  Line is ready for use.

2.  Removal of left IJ tunneled hemodialysis catheter.  Tip sent for culture.

INDICATION:  ___ with end-stage renal disease and MRSA bacteremia with
temporary line placed on ___.  Please tunnel line.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Drs. ___, Dr. ___ Dr. ___ attending
radiologist, performed the procedure.

PROCEDURE/FINDINGS: The risks and benefits of the procedure were explained to
the patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedure
timeout was performed.  The right neck was prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.

A ___ wire was advanced through the existing temporary hemodialysis catheter
into the IVC under fluoroscopic guidance, and the catheter was removed over
the wire. A ___ micropuncture sheath was advanced over the wire.
Attention was then directed towards creation of the subcutaneous tunnel. After
local anesthesia was provided to the upper chest and neck puncture site, the
subcutaneous tunnel was created with a blunt tunneling device.  The tunneled
hemodialysis catheter was pulled through the tunnel. The neck tract was
progressively dilated with 12- and ___ dilators and a ___ peel-
away sheath was then placed over the wire into the SVC.  The guide wire and
inner dilator were removed, and a ___ 23-cm tip-to-cuff dual-lumen
hemodialysis catheter was advanced through the sheath with its tip positioned
in the proximal right atrium.  The incision was closed with 0 Vicryl sutures,
and the catheter was secured to the skin with 0 silk sutures. A sterile
dressing was applied, and the catheter was flushed and heplocked. The patient
tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complications.

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of 80 mcg of
fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time of 45
minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a dual-lumen tunneled hemodialysis
catheter via the right internal jugular venous approach, with a tip-to-cuff
length of 23 cm, and the tip positioned in the proximal right atrium.  The
line is ready to use.
